study.question: Does removing the coordinate mean of the rank16 task context/history product improve click ranking, and does its effect depend on auxiliary adapter-context transfer?
study.hypothesis: Observed: the live-scale incumbent reaches click AUC0.6685268680; stopped-scale transfer reaches0.6670605582 and stopped-scale blocked0.6675728031, versus live blocked0.6678681339. Product beats additive fusion in earlier matched rows. Source inspection shows the incumbent RMS preserves a sample-dependent coordinate mean. Unmeasured mechanism hypothesis: that common component can consume normalized product energy and couple auxiliary updates across coordinates without useful click discrimination. Parameter-free mean removal may improve the remaining task-specific contrast while retaining live scale derivatives. The existence, size and harmfulness of a common component have not been observed in host telemetry; this is a falsifiable question, not an inferred diagnosis.

nearest_work.difference: Keep the full blockwise task-product model; replace only product-coordinate centering before RMS, crossed with the inherited context gradient gate.

Previous factorial stopped the scale derivative while preserving fixed-state predictions. Here retain all native derivatives and intentionally change representation invariance, introducing no new learned parameters.

Retain inherited target-conditioned local activation and Dice. The proposed normalization acts on the later task-conditioned low-rank context/history product, not on event attention weights; adapted benchmark is not an exact original DIN reproduction.

Pinned primary implementation lines263/273 and301/313 use affine LayerNorm after hub/broadcast residuals. Inspect that centering operation as a nearest normalization alternative; implement only non-affine per-sample coordinate centering on the existing rank16 product, with no hubs/broadcast/attention added. Original INFNet paper details unavailable, equivalence and priority unverified.

Pinned primary implementation lines176..183 applies LayerNorm before token mixing/FFNs. No token mixer or learned affine normalization is adopted; local comparison isolates mean removal in the current product.
Pinned primary implementation lines210..237 uses LayerNorm before token attention/FFN residuals. Sparse expansion/tokenization and attention are not adopted; capacity stays fixed.

study.proposed_difference: Let x=tanh(Q_t c) * mean_over_occupied_blocks[tanh(H_t [M*b_j,global_details])]. Incumbent U(x)=x/sqrt(mean(x^2)+1e-4). Replacement C(x)=(x-mean(x))/sqrt(mean((x-mean(x))^2)+1e-4). Means run only over the last rank16 axis per sample/task. Both paths execute with native derivatives and the unused path is multiplied by zero. Cross C/U with auxiliary adapter-context gate enabled/blocked; preserve all learned modules and initialization. C removes the constant-coordinate direction; no learned affine scale/bias. Empty-history corrections remain masked outside this operator.
predictions: At common nonzero interaction-output weights, uncentered cells match their corresponding live incumbent predictions/VJPs/one-step/Dice state; all cells retain the same parameter count. A mismatch invalidates comparison until fixed.

Centered product has zero coordinate mean and is invariant to adding a constant to x before normalization; the uncentered product generally is not. Constant x maps to zero under centering; all empty/zero cases stay finite.

If the proposed common-component interference matters, centered_transfer improves click AUC over uncentered_transfer; an auxiliary-transfer-specific mechanism predicts a larger centering gain with transfer enabled than blocked. No numeric improvement is promised.
Any candidate must exceed both frozen source bests at reported cost; report all four tasks because incumbent auxiliary AUC already trails DIN.
falsifiers: Centered_transfer failing to exceed its replay rejects useful centering for this implementation under the frozen recipe; a tiny isolated gain without repetition is preliminary.
No positive repeatable interaction rejects the stronger auxiliary-transfer-specific explanation even if centering has a main effect.
A gain eliminated by a retained-denominator/norm-matched follow-up supports scale/optimization instead of a specific offset-interference explanation.
Changed masking, gradients outside authorized routes, replay mismatch, new parameters or excess hard cost invalidate the intended controlled comparison.
alternative_explanations: The common coordinate mean may encode useful signal; removing it may lose click discrimination.
Centering changes RMS amplitude, Jacobian, dense clipping and sparse-optimizer trajectories together; improvement can arise from optimization rather than nuisance removal.
A learned rank basis can rotate useful information into the discarded direction; this is a restrictive inductive bias rather than extra expressivity.
Single-seed variation, extensive validation reuse and one-pass convergence can explain small gains.
Historical offline feedback and auxiliary label semantics may drive the click/auxiliary tradeoff; no production causal transfer is established.
